title: Maximum Score of Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Given a 2D integer array intervals, where each interval is defined by its start position li, end position ri, and weight weighti, select up to four non-overlapping intervals to maximize the total weight of their weights.
statement: Given a 2D integer array intervals, where each interval is defined by its start position li, end position ri, and weight weighti, select up to four non-overlapping intervals to maximize the total weight of their weights. Return the lexicographically smallest set of indices corresponding to these intervals. Intervals are considered non-overlapping if they do not share any points, even at the boundaries.
constraints: intervals has up to 50,000 inclusive [left,right,weight] entries with positive weights.
Choose at most four intervals that share no point, so the next start must exceed the previous end.
Maximize total weight and return the lexicographically smallest sorted list of original indices among ties.
hints: Sorting by start makes the next compatible interval a binary-search jump.
Use four bottom-up selection layers; each state compares skipping with taking and jumping past the current end.
Store total weight and a sorted index tuple, breaking equal-weight ties lexicographically.
The recurrence exhausts every compatible selection, while the tie comparison propagates the globally smallest optimal list.
